We started seeing a sharp increase in latency and 5xx errors across our inference endpoints around 07:35 PST this morning. Impact: customer-facing checkout feature times out for ~15% of requests; throughput for the day is down ~40%. Our ops team has collected traces and some 503/500 response samples — attaching a short log excerpt (bridge-log-20261219.txt).

Symptoms we observed:
- 07:35–08:00 PST: steep increase in tail latency for generation APIs (p95 up from 350ms -> 2.1s, p99 > 8s)
- Correlated spike in GPU OOM logs on the serving tier around 07:38

Attaching: bridge-log-20261219.txt (snippet), sample request IDs, and a screenshot of the errors.

- Raised autoscaler floor to avoid repeated scale-to-zero oscillations for high-concurrency jobs

Subject: RE: High latency + 500s across inference endpoints — incident findings and temporary fixes

Team / Alyssa — investigative update and preliminary RCA. Attaching full draft: FastRetail_RCA_v1.pdf and remediation-timeline.xlsx.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: a recent kernel selector change (deployed 2026-12-19 06:50 PST) caused an aggressive kernel that is incompatible with our mixed-precision quantized variant under certain sequence-length distributions. That kernel path raised GPU memory pressure leading to intermittent OOMs and eviction storms in the serving pool.
- Cascading effect: OOMs caused request retries and queue saturation, which manifested as increased tail latency and 500-series errors upstream. The autoscaler policy then oscillated due to misestimated arrival rates, amplifying the impact.

Actions taken so far (successful):
- 08:30 PST: Rolled back kernel selector to the prior stable build for affected pools (rollforward guarded by canary) — immediate improvement in error rate from 6% -> 0.9% within 18 minutes
- Raised autoscaler min replicas and increased warm pool for customer-specific capacity (temporary override)
- Applied request-level throttling for high-concurrency checkout path for 60 minutes to avoid queue saturation while rollout completed

Proposed corrective actions (short/medium term):
1) Patch: fix kernel selection heuristic to account for mixed-precision quantized models + sequence-length heuristics (dev ETA: 5 business days)
2) Autoscaler: improve arrival-rate smoothing and add a surge-protection cap to prevent oscillation (dev ETA: 3 business days)
3) Observability: ship per-customer GPU memory pressure dashboards and an alert rule for memory-pressure > 70% sustained (ops ETA: 2 business days)
4) Client-side mitigations: recommend conservative client-side batching for checkout (FastRetail ops) and graceful retry/backoff (docs: updated snippet in remediation spreadsheet)

Planned timeline: remediation-timeline.xlsx has dates and owners. We're targeting a code patch and controlled rollout by 2026-12-24 with validation tests and rollout canary over 48 hours.

Alyssa — can you confirm internal acceptance criteria for closure (e.g., <0.5% error rate sustained for 48h, p99 < 700ms for checkout traffic) and any blackout dates for patching?

Attachments: FastRetail_RCA_v1.pdf (draft, contains logs, sequence-length histograms, memory traces), remediation-timeline.xlsx (owners + dates)

Best,
David Kim
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: FastRetail — executive summary, ownership & closure checklist

Folks — updated executive note and closure checklist following David's RCA draft. This is being shared with our customer execs and our internal GTM/ops leads.

Executive summary (for leadership):
- Incident: kernel-selector regression caused GPU memory pressure -> OOMs -> retries -> queue saturation -> elevated latency and 5xx rates impacting checkout throughput.
- Business impact: FastRetail saw ~40% throughput loss during the window; potential revenue exposure for holiday peak.
- Containment/Recovery: rollback and warm-pool override returned error rate to acceptable threshold within ~20 minutes; temporary throttles reduced saturation risk.

Ownership & commitments:
- Engineering (David): code patch for kernel selector and unit/integration tests; target ship by 2026-12-24; owner: david_kim
- Autoscaling (Platform Infra): smoothing fix + surge cap; target ship by 2026-12-22; owner: michael_grant (coordination)
- Observability (Ops): per-customer GPU memory dashboards + alerts; target 2026-12-21; owner: laura_bennett
- Customer Liaison (CS/AM): weekly validation checks with FastRetail for 2 weeks post-rollout; owner: laura_bennett

Closure criteria (must be satisfied before we mark incident closed):
- Customer agrees to closure: confirmation that production behavior meets acceptance criteria (error rate < 0.5% for 48h, p99 < 700ms for checkout)
- Code patch deployed to production and validated in canary + ramp
- Post-deploy regression tests added to CI for similar kernel/quantization interactions
- Internal retro with lessons and action-owner assignment complete

Customer comms: Laura, please sync the remediation-timeline.xlsx to the FastRetail drive and propose a validation window with their SREs. Michael, iterate on the messaging to our execs; I've copied Alyssa so they have the exec-level commit.

Thanks everyone — keep the bridge notes consolidated in SRV-4210. I'll escalate to our CTO's office if we need additional credits/exec outreach.

Kimberly Park
VP, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
